item.description: Open in new tab

My research focuses on children’s moral behavior, such as cheating and lying. Particularly, I examine the role of the self in moral behavior across two main lines of work.

First: Children’s negative self-attitudes and moral development

I find that children’s dishonest behavior is not only related to cognitive, neural (Yu, Dai et al., 2025) and environmental factors, but also to how they perceive themselves. Children who exhibit higher self-criticism (Yu, Tay et al., 2026) and more dysfunctional self-related attitudes (Yu, Ding, & Hong, 2025) are more likely to engage in dishonest behavior. In these cases, dishonesty may function as a compensatory strategy to obtain external validation or as a protective strategy to avoid disapproval. In contrast, children in more supportive environments that enhance self-esteem tend to show higher levels of honesty (Yu, Zhang et al., in prep).
